utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish everybody a good afternoon, and the people in the public gallery. I would like to ask the registrar now to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, this is case number IT-03-72-I, the Prosecutor versus Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam. I wish to ask the parties for the appearances. Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the Prosecution are appearing Sabine Bauer and Alex Whiting. Ruth Karper, the case manager; and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUELLER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Good afternoon, thank you for welcoming us. The Defence is represented by my co-counsel Mr. Robert Fogelnest and by myself Peter Michael Mueller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like to ask Mr. Babic if he can hear me in a language he understands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, sir. I am Judge El Mahdi, Judge of the International Criminal Tribunal. This case has been assigned by an order of the President of the Tribunal to the first Chamber, a decision made by the President of the first Chamber, Chamber I. I have myself been assigned to this case in order to be the Judge for the initial appearance of the accused. I will briefly recall the procedure which has taken place up to now. First of all, the indictment was confirmed on the 17th of November, 2003, and as I have mentioned at the beginning, the order of the President assigning this case to Chamber number I is dated 26 November. On the same day, the President -- the Presiding Judge of the first Chamber assigned me to sit for the initial appearance of the accused. I would like to briefly explain what the case is about. First of all, this initial appearance. Initial appearance, as specified in Rule 62 in the Rules of Procedure in this Tribunal, which says: Plea, that the Chamber -- Trial Chamber or a Judge thereof must satisfy himself during the initial appearance that the right of the accused to have counsel has been respected, satisfy himself or herself that the right of the accused to counsel is respected. I see that counsel for the Defence are present, are here in the courtroom, so this condition has been fulfilled. The second duty is to read or have the indictment read to the accused in a language the accused understands and satisfy himself or herself that the accused understands the indictment. By the same token, I should also refer to the right of the accused, more specifically the fact that the accused has to be informed that after the indictment has been read to him with the charges against him, he may enter immediately a plea, he or she may have 30 days to enter a plea and say whether he pleads guilty or not guilty on one or more counts of the indictment. Therefore, I wanted all this to be quite clear from the beginning and that the rights of the accused are well understood. I will therefore request, before the reading of the indictment or the counts of the indictment, I would like to ask Mr. Babic to first of all let us have his name, place of birth, year of birth; his complete names, surname and name, and if necessary, the name of his father.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Milan Babic, son of Bozo, born on the 26th of February, 1956 in Kukar. I am by training a doctor of dental medicine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is precisely what we have here in the indictment. Before the indictment is read or before, rather, the counts of the indictment are read out, I would like to put Mr. Babic on notice about what these counts are about. The Prosecutor of the Tribunal alleges that Mr. Milan Babic is responsible and criminally responsible for those crimes which are represented by Articles 3 and 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal. Those are war crimes for Article 3, and crimes against humanity in Article 5. The facts or events took place between the 1st of August, 1991, until 15 February 1992. Broadly speaking, the indictment mentions, and I quote, under individual criminal responsibility, [In English] "Article 7(10 of the Statute of the Tribunal, Milan Babic is individually criminally responsible for the crimes referred to in Articles 3 and 5 of the Statute of the Tribunal and described in this indictment. The accused committed or otherwise aided and abetted in the planning, preparation, or execution of these crimes. By using the word 'committed' in this indictment, the Prosecutor does not intend to suggest that the accused physically committed any of the crimes charged personally. 'Committing' in this indictment refers to participation in a joint criminal enterprise as a co-perpetrator or an aider and abettor." [Interpretation] The indictment also speaks briefly about the events and the allegations against Mr. Babic, to confront him with five counts. Mr. Babic, you retain the right to have the whole indictment read out to you or, if you so prefer and if you have had the opportunity - and I think you did have the opportunity to see and peruse this indictment - maybe you will let the Chamber know whether it is necessary or not to go in detail through the whole indictment but only to let -- let us know and read out only the counts of the indictment which --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is not necessary to have the entire indictment read out to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Babic. I will, therefore, now ask for the counts to be read one after the other by the registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1: Persecutions on political, racial, and religious grounds, a crime against humanity, punishable under Articles 5(h) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you plead, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MR. FOGELNEST
utterances.text: May I address the Court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FOGELNEST
utterances.text: Please forgive me, this is my very first appearance in this room. It is an honour to appear before Your Honour. With respect to a plea, we would respectfully request that no plea be entered at this time, that Mr. Babic would stand mute, plead neither guilty or not guilty and that the procedures with respect to response to that be followed. We anticipate that the Court would enter a plea of not guilty on his behalf, but we have instructed him not to respond to that question at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. [Interpretation] Therefore, if I understand you rightly, Mr. Babic requests leave to have the 30 days time span before he will enter a plea of guilty or not guilty. Thank you. This being said, I will ask the registrar to read the indictment in order to satisfy myself that you have heard the charges alleged against you. Yes. So, Madam Registrar, would you please be so kind as to read out the counts of the indictment. Thank you very much. You can sit down, Mr. Babic. [In English] Count, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2: In relation to the conduct described in paragraph 15(a), murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3, and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 3: In relation to the conduct described in paragraph 15(b), cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 4: In relation to the conduct described in paragraph 15(d) wanton destruction of villages, or devastation not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(b) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal. Count 5: In relation to the conduct described in paragraph 15(d), destruction or wilful damage done to institutions dedicated to education or religion, a violation of the laws or customs of war as recognised by Common Article 3(1)(d) of the Geneva Conventions of 1949, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to remind Mr. Babic, as well as counsel, that Mr. Babic has 30 days following this initial appearance, that is from today, to enter a plea one way or the other. But since those 30 days will end during the end-of-year recess of the Tribunal and in order not to infringe Mr. Babic's rights, then the Chamber grants him until the 15th of January next year, 2004, to enter a plea and to let the Chamber know what is his position in respect to the charges which reproached him. If a party has any question on the Prosecutor's side, Madam, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, not to the initial appearance as such, not to the plea, but I have, of course, questions in relation to subsequent decisions of the Trial Chamber. It relates to the motions that were filed today, both by the Prosecution and the Defence, but these are matters that should be kept confidential and discussed in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, we may request the registrar to have a private session. Would that be enough, private session and not a closed session?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Registrar, please, we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. This having been said, I will let you know what my ruling is as soon as possible, and I believe we have no other matter to discuss now and, therefore, I close this hearing. The meeting is adjourned. In -- --- Break taken at 4.07 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, there appears to be a difficulty with the translation from French into English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Is it all right now? Can you hear us?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's all right now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you. So I have consulted with the Chamber, and I hereby order the detention on remand of the accused until further notice. A written decision will be issued tomorrow. Thank you to everybody. [Interpretation] The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: at 5.33 p.m.
